item.title: CJP's Das, Ranka try to sneak into Jantar Mantar, detained by Delhi Police
item.description: Members of the Cockroach Janta Party gathered at Jantar Mantar carrying the national flag. They aimed to protest against the current government led by Narendramodi. Abhijeet Dipke reported on social media that certain individuals, including Ashutosh Ranka, were detained. The police intervened and took party members into custody during the protest. This situation highlights ongoing tensions between the party and government authorities over resistance movements.
item.dc:creator: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI

item.title: Activist shot dead while exposing drug trade in Punjab; caught on social media live
item.description: Parwinder Singh Jhota was involved in a sting operation targeting a medical store in Mansa. He confronted the store owner about selling prohibited substances and had a heated exchange before being shot. Despite his attempts to escape, Jhota fell and was pronounced dead at the hospital. The police have identified the shooter, Ashwani Kumar, who fled after the incident.
item.dc:creator: NEEL KAMAL

item.title: Dad sold apartment, quit job; mom pledged gold: Making of India's latest WGM Sahithi
item.description: Sahithi Varshini Moogi’s journey to becoming India’s latest Woman Grandmaster is a story of many elements, with talent, sacrifice, and perseverance only part of it. Despite losing nearly three years to the pandemic and facing financial hardships and limited opportunities, she achieved the milestone with her father, Lokeswara Moogi Rao, as her coach. After selling property, pledging gold, and quitting his job, he continues pursuing her dream of chess greatness.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Zuckerberg gave Alexandr Wang $100 billion, then asked: ‘Are you sure this will work’
item.description: Mark Zuckerberg recently shared insights about his hefty investments in artificial intelligence, sparking debate over the technology’s viability. Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, suggested uncertainty may linger around research progress projected for late 2025. Despite initial hurdles, Meta's Muse AI app remarkably resonated with users, breaking download records post-launch.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Drone attack sinks ship off Bulgaria coast, second strike in a week
item.description: A drone assault near the Black Sea coast of Bulgaria led to one ship's sinking and damage to another. The Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3 was impacted, but all crew members were rescued unharmed. Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev labeled the attacks intolerable and emphasized maritime security concerns. Similar incidents were recorded earlier in the month, highlighting rising threats to commercial shipping.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Hyderabad techie dies after falling from 30th floor of his apartment
item.description: A 29-year-old software engineer from Suryapet district died by suicide at Golf Edge Apartments in Hyderabad. He had recently moved into a rented flat just two days before the incident occurred. A security guard found him on the ground and notified the residents of the apartment complex. He was later shifted to a private hospital, where he was declared dead.
item.dc:creator: MANVI VYAS

item.title: Girl, 15, turns bullying ordeal into mental health initiative for others
item.description: Aanya Mukherjee's journey through high school was marred by bullying that took a toll on her mental health and self-esteem. After a disappointing response from her initial school, she transferred to a more supportive environment that fostered her healing. Passionate about mental health, she founded a nonprofit and advocates for the inclusion of youth perspectives in these vital discussions.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.dc:creator: AADRITA HALDER

item.title: Indonesian conservationist, 14, plants thousands of mangroves to help communities
item.description: In Indonesia, young activist Harley Fatahillah Yodhaloka Sunoto is leading a passionate campaign for mangrove restoration and climate education. Through his Mangrove Warrior initiative, he has successfully planted thousands of seedlings in critical coastal regions, strengthening ecosystems and supporting local communities. By collaborating with mothers and organizations, Harley is educating on sustainable practices, with an ambitious goal of planting one million mangroves and launching educational programs nationwide.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Michael Dell-backed firm spent $375m upgrading Boca Raton resort; 40% condos sold
item.description: An impressive $875 million investment is set to transform The Boca Raton resort into a luxurious haven of residential condominiums. With around 40% of these high-end residences already reserved, pricing starts at $8.95 million and can exceed $20 million. This revitalization forms part of the resort's centennial celebrations scheduled for 2026, with construction commencing the same year and concluding by 2029.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Sydney’s Opal Tower declared defect-free nearly 8 years after cracks forced evacuation
item.description: After nearly eight years of uncertainty, Sydney's Opal Tower has officially been declared defect-free, following significant structural issues uncovered in December 2018. This crisis led to evacuations, extensive repairs, and legal conflicts regarding the building's safety standards. Most residents have safely returned after comprehensive rectification processes, and property owners will receive compensation along with a 20-year structural warranty.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Zoho’s Sridhar Vembu tells staff no hike this year, tries to avoid layoffs
item.description: Sridhar Vembu, founder of Zoho, announced that employees will not receive annual salary hikes this year. This decision arises from increased costs associated with artificial intelligence and geopolitical challenges. Zoho has reduced its marketing budget and has not increased its headcount for 18 months. Vembu expressed gratitude for employees' understanding during this difficult period as he aims to avoid mass layoffs.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Meet Harrison Nott, 16, whose bedroom towel business now makes £750,000 a year
item.description: Harrison Nott, a 16-year-old entrepreneur from Essex, England, started CoolTowel in his bedroom in 2023. After winning a global pitching competition and attracting investor Rio Ferdinand, his cooling towel business generated over £750,000 in revenue this year. Despite sales success, stock shortages, copycats and operating costs remain challenges as he pursues profitability full-time.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: HCLTech jumps 7%, TCS up 5%: Why are IT stocks rallying
item.description: Dalal Street saw a surge as IT stocks soared following strong quarterly earnings from industry giants. HCLTech and Tata Consultancy Services were at the forefront, with their share prices climbing significantly. However, this rally comes amidst a tougher year for IT stocks, which have dipped by 23%. Investor concerns remain about inflation and fluctuating crude oil prices, with the global tech landscape also impacted by chip industry developments.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Ronaldo scores amid Riyadh security scare to close in on 1,000 career goals
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo edged closer to the monumental milestone of 1,000 career goals by netting a goal for Al-Nassr in their AFC Champions League match. Although security alerts caused a postponement against Neftchi Fergana, which caused discomfort among fans and players, Al-Nassr clinched a 3-1 victory with Ronaldo being instrumental. A pending dispute with the Portuguese Football Federation, however, looms over him.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Naomi Osaka reveals how daughter Shai changed her life beyond tennis
item.description: Naomi Osaka has opened up about her mental health struggles, crediting motherhood and her daughter, Shai, with helping her find happiness beyond tennis. The four-time Grand Slam champion revealed how her perspective has changed since her 2021 French Open withdrawal, when she disclosed her battle with depression and anxiety. After defeating Maria Timofeeva at the China Open, Osaka reflected on personal growth, gratitude and learning to balance her professional career with life outside tennis.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Madras HC upholds TN Speaker's acceptance of resignations of 6 AIADMK MLAs
item.description: The Madras high court ruled that the resignations of six AIADMK MLAs were valid and voluntary. The speaker's acceptance of the resignations was deemed constitutionally appropriate under the Tenth Schedule. The court clarified that resignation and disqualification are separate constitutional processes within the governing framework. Additionally, it mandated the speaker to resolve pending disqualification proceedings within two months.
item.dc:creator: SURESHKUMAR

item.title: Sarah, first Zimbabwean female umpire in Women's T20 WC, passes away at 36
item.description: Former Zimbabwe cricketer and umpire Sarah Dambanevana has died in Harare at 36 after months in hospital following a medical procedure. She represented Zimbabwe from 2009 to 2014 before becoming an international umpire. In 2023, she became the first Zimbabwean woman to officiate a World Cup final and later worked at the 2024 and 2025 women's World Cups.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Tenant's Rs 10L deposit claim fails; Delhi HC orders payment for unauthorised stay
item.description: The case involved a tenant, who rented a 238.38 sq. ft shop in 2014 from a couple in Delhi. The agreed monthly rent was Rs 25,500. However, the 11-month rent agreement was never registered. The tenant subsequently claimed that he had paid the landlords Rs 10 lakh in cash as a security deposit between November 2016 and March 2017.

item.title: India's economic story in fast lane, IMF projects 7% GDP growth for FY26 and FY27
item.description: India is projected to maintain a robust growth rate of 7% in both 2026 and 2027, bolstered by strong domestic demand and a thriving services sector, according to the International Monetary Fund. Positive revisions from the World Bank and OECD highlight resilience amid consumption patterns. However, challenges such as rising energy prices and geopolitical tensions could impact this trajectory, yet India's economic growth remains strong compared to other major nations.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Bought Maruti Invicto, found repainted parts; commission orders Rs 3.6 lakh relief
item.description: In a significant ruling, a consumer commission in Kerala has mandated Popular Vehicles & Services Ltd to replace a Maruti Invicto car due to undisclosed repainted parts before delivery. Evidence indicated the vehicle had sustained damage, leading to unexpected repair costs. With the dealer unresponsive to the buyer's complaints, the commission deemed this a clear deficiency of service and directed compliance within 30 days.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH THAKUR

item.title: Asian Para Games: Coach row, court battles, clearance delays deepen chaos
item.description: As the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games approaches, India faces significant challenges concerning athlete selections and administrative delays. Recent disputes regarding the omission of key coaches from the para shooting contingent have created unrest among athletes. Delayed approvals for several disciplines have further complicated preparations, impacting kit distribution and athlete readiness. Athletes from badminton and table tennis confront last-minute issues just days before their events begin.
item.dc:creator: SABI HUSSAIN

item.title: New Zealand-based stepsons shoot UP trader dead over mother’s 2nd marriage; CCTV emerges
item.description: Navjot Singh, a 30-year-old trader, was shot dead inside his shop in Kumhariya Tah village on Saturday. CCTV footage captured two masked men arriving in a silver Maruti Alto before the attack. His father believes his stepsons conspired to kill him due to personal disputes over their mother's marriage. The police are currently searching for the two absconding suspects involved in the murder.
item.dc:creator: KRISHNA CHAUDHARY

item.title: Eating olive oil before carbs may curb blood sugar spikes: Study
item.description: Findings from Kyoto University suggest that the sequence of consuming fats before carbohydrates might significantly impact blood sugar management. In studies involving mice, researchers noted that olive oil effectively delayed gastric emptying, thereby lessening spikes in blood glucose. However, this research remains untested on humans, indicating the need for additional clinical trials. It's essential for diabetic patients to maintain their existing dietary practices and treatments.
item.dc:creator: TIMESOFINDIA.COM

item.title: Why Saudi Arabia's $83 billion military fails to deter Houthis despite advanced arsenal
item.description: Yemen's Houthi rebels conducted a series of missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia's critical infrastructure. The assault on King Khalid International Airport resulted in 13 fatalities and over 300 injuries. Despite substantial defense spending, Saudi Arabia struggles to effectively counter these threats using sophisticated military capabilities. Challenges include coordination issues and the asymmetric nature of the conflict with low-cost Houthi weapons.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: 'Not a single drop': AI data centre boom sparks water protests on Indonesian island
item.description: Around 300 residents of Batam island protested against water shortages that disrupted their daily lives. They accused data centres of depleting local freshwater resources amidst the ongoing water crisis. The local water utility has promised improvements, but concerns continue to grow regarding water access. Authorities have instructed data centre companies to establish their own desalination plants to alleviate pressure on reservoirs.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: ‘He is watching from above’: Lalremsiami’s emotional tribute to her late father
item.description: Lalremsiami Hmarzote made history by clinching gold at the Asian Games in women's hockey, a pivotal accomplishment for her and her team. She scored vital goals, particularly in the final against China. Remembering her late father, who was her source of motivation, Hmarzote is now determined to inspire young girls in Mizoram to take up hockey and chase their sporting dreams as the Indian women's team eyes the Olympics.

item.title: Drinks, hotel, high speed: What we know about Kerala’s Mini Cooper crash; all held
item.description: A devastating accident on Airport Road led to the arrest of four college students after their Mini Cooper collided with a scooter, resulting in the death of three people. Evidence suggests that the driver was under the influence at the time of the incident. The excise department is now looking into bars that supplied alcohol to the group, raising significant concerns over irresponsible drinking and driving.

item.title: India No. 1 Nagal apologises to local Portuguese crowd for post-match gesture
item.description: Sumit Nagal apologised to the Maia crowd and Portuguese player Henrique Rocha for making a “talking gesture” after his hard-fought first-round win at the Maia ATP Challenger. Nagal called it a heat-of-the-moment reaction and confirmed he had apologised personally to Rocha. The incident comes after India's disappointing Asian Games tennis campaign ended without a medal for the first time since 1986.
